found_before_measuring: journey-run.mjs JOURNEYS['jrn02-first-hour'] exists (216000 frames, durationMin 60) and cadence.mjs/competence.mjs are built and hardened over four rounds — but no code anywhere drives an hour of play. driveBeats() drives the OPENING (first input, first control, a still window, the census walk) and then runs the remaining budget out with `stepAndSample(handle, min(o.frames, 20000))` and zero inputs. journeyLegs() branches on jrn03..jrn08 and has no jrn02 case. So a jrn02 run today = the opening + 5.5 minutes of nobody playing, capped at 20000 frames regardless of --duration-min.

Consequence if that had been trusted: cadence.mjs would have reported gap_max ~= the whole run and combat_fraction 0 — HF3 twice over — as a fact about the BUILD, when it is a fact about the DRIVER. Same shape as the 36,000-frame/0-event session (empty ops.json).
findings: F1 — NOTHING DRIVES jrn02. journey-run.mjs registers the journey but driveBeats() ends with stepFrames(min(frames,20000)) and zero inputs, and journeyLegs() has no jrn02 branch. A jrn02 run today is the opening plus 5.5 minutes of nobody playing, whatever --duration-min says.

F2 — THE VERB LEDGER IS UNMEASURABLE FROM THE TRACE. RI-JRN02 M-I1 needs `input_action` (A-JRN7) per verb. Measured, with three controls all holding in the same browser: the drain is live; 10 of 16 actions produced their own consequence event so the button reached the body; and `input_action` IS reachable and IS carried (proved by pressing `interact` standing at a signpost, which put input_action in the record and opened the post). Against that positive control, 0 of 16 actions emit `input_action`, and SEVEN of them — light, roll, block, parry, jump, swap_right, swap_left — demonstrably EXECUTED (ACTION_START / GUARD_UP in the same window) and still emitted none.

F2 cause: the only emission for a combat button is game/src/sim/player.js:109, inside stepPlayer(), which nothing imports — game/src/sim/souls.js:46 says so in-tree ("DEAD CODE. Nothing imports stepPlayer"). The live path is game/src/combat/player.js and it contains no input_action emit at all. Two parallel implementations of one system, RULES 10.

F3 — input_action IS emitted on five engine.js paths, all of them the `interact` reach, but the harness-verb arm of that route emits OUTSIDE the fixed step and sim/step.js clears the bus at the top of the step, so signRead() raises the event and no record ever carries it. Only the BUTTON arm lands in the trace. Recorded as two arms in the artifact rather than one number.

F4 — COMBAT ARRIVES AT MINUTE 1.5, NOT MINUTE 19. §A puts `light` at first_use <= 0:19 and `roll` at <= 0:19. The agent, which presses a combat verb only when the world puts a hostile in reach, first swung at 1:31 and first rolled at 3:00. The bars are upper bounds so the letter is met, but the Souls half of the hour arrives seventeen minutes ahead of the sheet and nothing else in the corpus would notice.

F5 — THE ORDINARY TRASH MOB CANNOT BE LEARNED ON AVERAGE. `inf_trash` declares startups of 22, 44, 54 and 68 frames — a 46-frame spread against an 11-frame i-frame window. An agent that learns ONE repeated attack goes 0.833 -> 1.000; the same agent against the full declared moveset is FLAT at 0.167, because no single roll time covers the spread and the mean covers none of them. This is the right shape for a Souls moveset — you learn the moves, not the mean — and it is a warning about §C itself: K2 averaged over an encounter will read a perfectly learnable enemy as unlearnable.
done: tools/journey/jrn02-hour.mjs — three modes. --verb-coverage (the instrument audit), --hour (the driver that did not exist), --self-test (11 offline assertions, all green, including two that prove the gap statistic goes red on a dead hour and STAYS red on an hour of uncorroborated dodge-rolling).
tools/journey/jrn02-competence.mjs — RI-JRN02 §C as a 6-arm design that can fail. 11 offline assertions.

THE HOUR NOW EXISTS AS A DRIVEN RUN. Need-driven policy agent, walking the `crossing` road route out of Lilmoth. At the 9.0-minute checkpoint: 1,602 m walked, 7 verbs acquired in a WORLD-DRIVEN order — sprint@0.03, interact@0.73, read@0.73, light@1.52, roll@3.0, lock_on@7.37, use_item@8.38. That order matches V3 (light -> roll -> block -> lock_on -> use_item -> heavy) with `block` and `heavy` not yet triggered.

COMPETENCE: all four controls hold. B (learner on, one repeated attack) 0.833 -> 1.000; A (learner FROZEN) flat at 0 — the delete-the-fix bites; D (randomised enemy) ends at 0.5 against B's 1.0; E (unlearnable, spread >> i-frames) flat — the hard control.
method_notes: THE COMPETENCE DESIGN, defended in the file header. §C cannot be answered as written on this build: the agent is a program, so authoring a better late policy measures my source code, and holding the policy fixed (as M-I9 gear and K7 tier require) makes the expected improvement zero by construction. The design gives the agent ONE thing it cannot be told and can only learn by being hit — the enemy's windup — and identical code runs in every arm. I authored the capacity to learn, not the content learned; the content came from the world.

THREE CONTROLS I WATCHED FAIL BEFORE THEY PASSED, each recorded in the file that carries it: (1) the verb-coverage audit refused to report 0/16 until it could show, in the same browser, that it could hear an input_action at all; (2) the competence control "a randomised enemy is unlearnable" FAILED — the learner converged on the distribution mean and gained 0.167, because an 11-frame i-frame window is wide relative to the spread. Bar made relative and a genuinely unlearnable arm E added; (3) the relative-delta bar was then CEILING-CONFOUNDED — arm B reaches 0.833 in its first bout, so it can gain at most 0.167 while arm D climbs 0.5 to a worse end state. The statistic is now the end state and both numbers are published.

TWO FIXTURE BUGS FOUND BY THE DRIVER FAILING, not by inspection: the first loop walked only when no verb had fired, so `sprint` fired once and starved locomotion for ever (3.7 simulated minutes, body moved 2.6 m, 25 jump presses). And `walkPath` beelines, so the body wedged against Lilmoth's buildings; locomotion is now `walkRoute` along the built road legs. Either would have published "the first hour contains nothing" as a finding about the game.
not_done: THE 60-MINUTE RUN DID NOT FINISH INSIDE MY BUDGET. It reached 9.0 simulated minutes at the last checkpoint I read and was still running at hand-off, writing dispatches.jsonl and samples.jsonl every tick and hour.json every 60 ticks. Throughput is about 2 simulated minutes per 5 minutes of wall clock, so a full hour is roughly 2h15m. Every hour-derived number above is A NINE-MINUTE NUMBER and is labelled as one. V_exercised 6/14 and gap_max 496 s are NOT verdicts on the hour and must not be quoted as such.

cadence.mjs WAS NOT RUN over the produced trace. It is built, hardened over four rounds, and reads trace.jsonl — which this driver only writes at the END of the run, so there was nothing for it to read. That is the single most valuable next step and it is one command.

C5..C8 (combat/dialogue/traversal/menu fractions) are only approximated driver-side at tick resolution in hour.json, and are labelled `fractions_driver_side`. cadence.mjs owns them and its own round-4 note says no trace record in this tree carries a `ui` subtree at all, so C6 and C8 are very likely unmeasurable — unconfirmed by me.
M-I3 (verb teaching purity, V2 "no verb is introduced by text") NOT RUN. It needs the UI-text stream, which journey-run.mjs owns and this driver does not sample. HF2 is therefore unassessed.
M-I5 (necessity: re-run each introducing encounter WITHOUT the verb) NOT RUN. `--no-acquire` exists and is self-tested as the arm that would do it, but no encounter was re-run.

M-I13 / M-N1..M-N5 (the frustration ledger and the naive pass) NOT RUN. They require a naive agent under enforced isolation, which is a separate fleet role (JC-02N) and not a builder's to run on itself.

caveat_the_gap_numbers_inherit_F2: gap_max 496 s and gap_p95 477 s must NOT be read as C1/C2 verdicts, and the reason is F2. C1 counts an input only when the trace CORROBORATES one of its five world-facts within a second, and the trace cannot see fifteen of the sixteen buttons — so only 3 of 135 dispatched actions could be corroborated at all. The gap statistic is therefore measuring the instrument's blindness, not the hour's emptiness. C1/C2 are UNMEASURABLE on this build until `input_action` reaches the live combat path, and that is the honest reading. By contrast combat_fraction 0.223 is computed from entity proximity, not from inputs, so it does NOT inherit F2 — and it sits inside C5's 0.12-0.30 band, which is the first evidence anywhere that this hour is neither the walking simulator nor the arena of How-we-lose #1 and #2.
